page.layout: One column of running text, with a centred sub-heading "Exempla," in the middle of the page. No marginal notes. Below the last full line, at the right, the catchword.

main_text.p: 2. Cum sumitur accidentarium pro causa perse.

3. Cum ponitur no adæquata pro adæquata: mediata pro immediata: vel voluntaria cum naturali: vel contra: efficiens per veram actionem cum efficiente per naturalem quandam consecutionem, vel contra: confunditur.
4. Cum causæ insufficientes tanquam efficaces assumuntur: ut, cum una adhibetur causa, ubi adhibendæ erant plures.
5. Cum plures ponuntur causæ pro una.
6. Cum perverRuntur genera causarum: ut, cum finalis dicitur, quæ est impulsiva efficiens, vel efficiens, quæ est formalis aut materialis.
7. Cum id quod ex accidenti convenit causæ, transfertur etiam ad effectum.
main_text.head: Exempla,
main_text.p: 1. Accidit medico, qui est vera causa sanitatis, esse Theologum. Jam si quis dicat: Theologum ægroto restituisse sanitatem, is committit fallaciam a non causa tanquam causa, quia ponit accidens causæ, quod nihil agit pro propria dicta causa.
Causa sine qua non, quæ vulgo dicitur, nomine, non re causa est. Itaq; à rectius loquentibus conditio sine qua non vocatur. Hanc

page.notes: The first line "2." appears to begin the page without a running heading above it on the scan; the header line "RODOLF. GOCLENII" is the running head and the page number 46 is read from the head, with some doubt on the final digit. The sub-heading "Exempla," is set in larger spaced type and is treated as a level 2 heading. The line "perRuntur" in item 6 is an uncertain reading of "pervertuntur" and may be [?]. The word "accidens" in item 1 and "adæquata" in item 3 are clear enough but the line is slightly faded. The catchword "si quis" is at the foot, right-aligned, and is not repeated in the text.
